subject: Request: temporary SLO concession + commercial carveout for Veridian pilot
messages:
From: Ava Rosen <ava.rosen@veridianbio.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@veridianbio.com>, procurement@veridianbio.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot SLO ask — network constraints at our sites

Hi Rafael / Lauren,

Thanks again for the great demo last week. We're excited to move to the 3-month pilot for our genomic-reporting pipeline. One thing that's come up with our infrastructure team: several of our lab sites route traffic through legacy NAT stacks that add tail latency during peak ingest windows.

Our procurement/legal team has asked whether Redwood can agree to a temporary, mutually‑agreed SLO concession while we finish network upgrades. Specifically:
- Reduce the uptime target for the pilot from 99.95% to 99.5% (six weeks from go‑live, then reassess)
- Service credit schedule while the concession is in effect (we proposed a 5% monthly credit if monthly availability < 99.5%)
- A modest commercial concession (one‑time pilot discount and committed capacity discount during remediation) to account for increased engineering risk

We need firm terms to put in our PO and to route for legal review. Can Redwood sign off on a limited-scope SLO variance plus a short commercial carveout? If so, what approvals are required and what will the exact wording look like?

Attached: our SLO request memo and current procurement template.

Thanks,
Ava Rosen
Director, IT Procurement
Veridian Biotech

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pilot SLO ask — network constraints at our sites

Folks — forwarding Veridian's request. Key asks (summary): temporary SLO target from 99.95% -> 99.5% for the pilot window, a simple monthly credit if availability dips below the concession, plus a short commercial discount on committed capacity during the remediation window.

Commercial team: can we offer the pilot discount (they asked for "modest") and a short-term committed capacity discount without setting a precedent for larger customers?

Risk/ops: is 99.5% acceptable operationally for a 3-month pilot limited to EU+US staging clusters? We will require telemetry and a remediation plan.

Proposed internal ask for exec approval:
- Approve temporary SLO variance: 99.5% uptime for up to 6 months; automatic reversion to contractual 99.95% thereafter unless extended by written agreement.
- Service credit: 5% of monthly invoice if monthly availability < 99.5% (credit applies only during variance window). Cap credits at 50% of that month's invoice.
- Commercial: 15% discount on committed capacity charges for the first 3 months of the pilot (to be reflected in the term sheet).

I recommend we escalate for Ben's signoff given this touches SLO terms and a non-standard commercial carveout. Veridian is strategic — pilot likely leads to enterprise deal if successful.

Rafael
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: veridian_slo_request.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot SLO ask — network constraints at our sites

Thanks for the summary, Rafael. I reviewed Veridian's memo and their procurement template. I'm comfortable approving a narrow, time‑boxed variance with the following controlled conditions:

1) Scope & duration
- Variance: lower uptime SLO = 99.5% (monthly measurement) for a maximum of 6 months from go‑live.
- Variance applies only to pilot deployment clusters explicitly listed in the term sheet (we'll enumerate by cluster IDs/regions).

2) Service credit schedule (applies only during variance window)
- If availability for a month < 99.5%: 5% credit of that month's Redwood invoice.
- If availability for a month < 98.0%: 15% credit of that month's Redwood invoice.
- Credit cap: 50% of the affected month's invoice.

3) Commercial concession
- One‑time pilot discount: 15% off committed capacity charges for the first 3 months.
- No change to overage pricing or reservoir caps.

4) Controls & prerequisites (non‑negotiable)
- Veridian must provide network remediation milestones (dates and owners) and agree to a twice‑weekly sync during the variance window.
- Redwood requires instrumented telemetry (tail latency dashboards) and access to relevant logs for debugging (read‑only).
- Variance void if Veridian routes non‑production traffic through public proxies not disclosed in the term sheet.

5) Legal/finance notes
- Marissa, please ensure the term sheet language matches the above and that the variance is explicitly flagged as a pilot-only exception that does not modify the master SLA. Finance: revenue recognition to reflect the one‑time discount.

If no objections by EOD Friday I authorize Rafael to accept these terms with Veridian and to circulate the draft term sheet for signature.

Ben Carter
VP, Deal Desk & Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Rosen <ava.rosen@veridianbio.com>, Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@veridianbio.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@veridianbio.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot SLO ask — network constraints at our sites

Hi Ava / Tom — thank you for the memo and for the transparency on remediation timelines. Ben has approved a narrow pilot variance with conditions; below is the agreed language we will include in the pilot term sheet. This is limited to the explicitly listed pilot clusters and will revert to standard SLA terms at the end of the variance window unless extended in writing.

Agreed pilot variance (summary):
- Uptime target during pilot: 99.5% monthly availability (max 6 months from pilot go‑live).
- Service credits while variance is active:
  • Monthly availability < 99.5%: 5% credit of that month's Redwood invoice.
  • Monthly availability < 98.0%: 15% credit of that month's Redwood invoice.
  • Credit cap: 50% of the affected month's invoice.
- Commercial concession: 15% discount on committed capacity charges for the first 3 months of the pilot.
- Preconditions: Veridian must provide a remediation milestone plan and grant read‑only access to relevant telemetry/logs. Twice‑weekly operational sync required.
- Clause: This pilot variance is a temporary, pilot‑only exception and does not amend the Master Services Agreement (MSA).

Next steps:
1) Marissa will prepare the term sheet language and the short addendum reflecting the variance.
2) Rafael to circulate DocuSign link for signature once procurement confirms PO details.
3) Technical kickoff to be scheduled after signatures — please propose dates next week.

I'm attaching the draft term sheet and pilot runbook. If procurement needs alternate credit thresholds or a different cap, please flag now so we can iterate quickly.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
